title: File Relay 多目标：成功/失败/重试/取消/Hub 重启 与 目标离线恢复（含 UI 反馈）

cases.title: File Relay 多目标 → 成功、失败、重试、取消、Hub 重启均正确
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PARTIAL excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: multi-target File Relay over the real product data path + Hub restart
description: Multi-target SUCCESS/FAILURE isolation: a two-target transfer where one target succeeded (exact source size/sha256/mode on disk) and the other failed (symlink destination rejected by the native host adapter) reached overall FAILED without blocking the good target.
RETRY: the failed target was retried individually (POST /api/transfers/<id>/retry?target_id=<node>) to SUCCESS with the exact source sha256.
CANCEL: a staged transfer whose target was offline was canceled -> terminal CANCELED, no destination file and the Hub staged blob/part cleaned.
HUB RESTART: the transfer staged while the target was offline survived the authorised repair-Hub restart and completed after reconnect with no half product.
UI readback: the /transfers page lists the owned rows and the rendered per-target statuses agree with the API (multi-target row 成功 with tgt_a 成功 + tgt_b 成功; cancel row 已取消).

remaining_or_limitations: The multi-target transfer uses the same source Agent for every target and a symlink destination as the deterministic failure; no cross-source case is included.
One Hub restart was performed (the single authorised repair unit).

cases.title: Hub 重启、Agent 重连、目标离线后的传输恢复
cases.canonical_before: NOT_RUN (repair build not executed; legacy baseline PARTIAL excluded per remaining_dimensions)

covered_dimensions.layer: repair-Hub restart / Agent reconnect / offline target / UI feedback
description: The source uploaded and the Hub staged the blob while the target was offline; the transfer row survived the ONE authorised repair-Hub restart unchanged.
The source Agent reconnected by itself after the restart; the target reconnected when brought back and ResumeNode delivered exactly once.
No destination file or temp file existed on the target while it was offline (before and after the restart), and the final file matched the exact source size/sha256/mode with the Hub staging cleaned.
All 4 protected repair nodes plus the primary :8080 Hub and every Agent kept their MainPIDs; only the repair-Hub MainPID changed, and /healthz, /readyz returned 200.
UI feedback is consistent with the API state for the owned transfers.

remaining_or_limitations: The Hub outage observed is short (unit stop/start, ~1-3 s); a long outage beyond the Agent heartbeat timeout was not exercised.
The UI stage is a read-only readback of the transfers table; no transfer was created or acted on from the UI.

harness_seams.authority: management and agent data-plane writes only to repair http://192.168.100.209:18080
harness_seams.hub_restart: only nodesteer-hub-repair-20260930-101945.service was stopped/started once; nodesteer-hub.service (:8080) and all Agent units untouched
harness_seams.owned_children: source on native-1, targets on native-2/native-3, exact repair Agent binary d55dc5cd..., each behind its own harness frame proxy
harness_seams.ui: agent-browser read-only session on the repair UI; no UI writes
harness_seams.credential_source: each child's own store (identity.credential), never a protected Agent config

attempts: evidence/attempt01-ui-assertion-bug/ : the first attempt produced correct UI data but its UI assertion was mis-specified - it looked for the transfer UUID in the rows, which the transfers table never renders. The owned row was in fact present with the correct rendered statuses (src-multi.bin -> 成功, tgt_a 成功 tgt_b 成功; src-cancel.bin -> 已取消). The assertion was corrected to match the rendered columns and the case verdict was coupled to the UI result, then the batch was re-run with a fresh nonce.
post_run_addendum.note: across all attempts only nodesteer-hub-repair-20260930-101945.service was ever stopped/started; the primary :8080 Hub (MainPID 1251) and every Agent unit kept their MainPID the whole time. No credential is persisted in any evidence file.
